summary: Hajime Sakurabe specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University (PhD 1944–1967) under Issai Funahashi and Susumu Yamaguchi, later serving on its faculty from 1949 to 1996, and at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1956–1958).

Hajime Tanabe was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida. He held academic posts at Tohoku University (~1913–1919) and Kyoto University (~1919–1945).

Hakuju Ui was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Junjirō Takakusu at the University of Tokyo and Richard von Garbe at Tübingen, later holding posts at Tokyo, Tohoku, Waseda, Komazawa, and Nagoya universities.
Halle O'Neal works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Kansas (~2005–2011) under the supervision of Sherry Fowler.

Hammalawa Saddhatissa worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Vidyodaya Pirivena, Banaras Hindu University, and the University of Edinburgh (PhD). His posts included London Buddhist Vihara (1957–1990), Vikramashila Pirivena, Mahabodhi College, and the University of Toronto.
Hank Glassman is a scholar in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He served as a faculty member at Haverford College, with his affiliation attested in 2009 and 2019.

Hanns Oertel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Yale University under William Dwight Whitney. He held positions at Yale (1891–1917), the University of Basel (1920), the University of Marburg (~1920–1925), and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (1925–1935).
Hannu Riikonen studied at the University of Helsinki from ~1967 to 1978. He later served as a professor at the University of Helsinki from ~1999 to 2013.

Hans Hartog studied Indology and linguistics across Tübingen, Bethel, and Munich before earning his PhD at the University of Marburg (1937–1939) under Friedrich Heiler. His teachers included Walther Wüst, Hanns Oertel, and Ferdinand Sommer.

Hans Henrich Hock is a linguist and Indologist who completed his studies at Yale University (~1967–1971). He spent his career as a professor of linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign from ~1969 to 2013.

Hans T. Bakker works in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Jacob Ensink and served at the University of Groningen from ~1982 to ~1995, later working as a curator at the British Museum (~2014–2019).
Hans-Werner Köhler is an Indologist who completed his doctoral studies under the supervision of Ernst Waldschmidt (attested 1973) and also studied under Eduard Hermann.

Hanung Kim specializes in Tibetology and history and archaeology. Kim earned a master's degree from Columbia University and a PhD from Harvard University under the doctoral supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.

Hara Prasad Sastri worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (attested 1905) and as Joint Philological Secretary at the Asiatic Society (attested 1905–1911).

Harald Hauptmann specialized in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Heidelberg University, he held posts at Heidelberg University (~1980–2001), DAI Istanbul (~1994–2001), and the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1989–2018).

Haraprasad Shastri was an Indologist and historian who studied at Sanskrit College and University and Presidency University, Kolkata. He held posts at Hare School, Presidency University, Sanskrit College and University (~1895–1908), and the University of Dhaka (~1921–1924).

Hari Damodar Velankar was an Indologist who studied under H. M. Bhadkamkar. He held positions at Wilson College, Mumbai (attested 1944) and served as Joint Director at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (attested 1959–1960).

Hari Shankar Prasad works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and was taught by Ramakant Tripathi, with Jan Willem de Jong serving as his doctoral supervisor.

Haridas Bhattacharyya was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta. He held academic posts at the University of Calcutta (~1917–1921), University of Dhaka (~1921–1947), and Banaras Hindu University (~1948–1952).
Haridas Sinharay was an Indologist who held a post at Maulana Azad College, with appointments attested in 1970 and 1990.
